content: The king has fed us well; there is still fat around the roots of my heart.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Þormóðr Kolbrúnarskáld at the Battle of Stiklestad (Heimskringla)
explanation: Mortally wounded in the chest by an arrow at the Battle of Stiklestad, the court skald Þormóðr drew the iron point from his own flesh, noticed the clinging yellow fat, and spoke these final words with calm wit before expiring. It represents the pinnacle of northern equanimity: greeting inescapable death not with trembling terror, but with gratitude, loyalty, and dry wit.
practicalInsight: Bring humor and calm grace to stressful circumstances today. Refuse to let panic rob you of your poise.
reflectionPrompt: When severe trials hit your life, does fear seize your spirit, or can you maintain dignity and a grounded perspective?
